channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: 10 Hectares of Agricultural Land Worth 113 Million Som Returned to State
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region, 10 hectares of agricultural land valued at nearly 113 million som have been returned to state ownership. The Prosecutor's Office discovered that officials illegally transferred the land to private ownership in 2005. Similar land reclamations have occurred in other districts of the Issyk-Kul region, involving significant areas and values.

item.title: Uzbekistan, Oman, and Iran Foreign Ministers Hold Talks in Muscat
item.description: The Foreign Ministers of Uzbekistan, Oman, and Iran convened for a trilateral meeting in Muscat. Discussions focused on expanding trade and economic cooperation, strengthening transport and logistics ties, and enhancing the transit potential of the three nations. The ministers also addressed the regional situation, emphasizing diplomatic solutions and constructive dialogue for peace and stability.

item.title: IMF Recommends Gradual Increase in Kazakhstan's Utility Tariffs
item.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has recommended a gradual increase in Kazakhstan's utility tariffs. The IMF suggests a transparent and understandable system for setting tariffs, based on the actual costs of service providers and long-term planning. This approach would allow utility companies to fund infrastructure upgrades while preventing sudden price hikes for consumers. The IMF also cautioned that rising tariffs could fuel inflation.

item.title: Kazakhfilm National Film Studio Appoints New Permanent Head After Two Years
item.description: The Shaken Aimanov Kazakhfilm National Film Studio has appointed a new permanent president, Kurmanbek Zhumagali, for the first time in two years. Zhumagali previously managed budgets at the Center for Support of National Cinema. The position had been vacant since July 2024.

item.title: Millions of Foreigners Entered Kazakhstan in Nine Months, Led by Three Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan recorded millions of foreign entries during the first nine months of the year. The majority of these visitors originated from three specific countries, indicating significant cross-border movement. Further details on the nationalities and purpose of these visits were not provided in the initial report.

item.title: Airbus Forecasts Triple Passenger Traffic Growth in Central Asia by 2045
item.description: Airbus anticipates a threefold increase in passenger traffic within Central Asia by the year 2045. This projection highlights the region's growing importance in global aviation. The forecast suggests significant expansion in air travel demand across the Central Asian states over the next two decades.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Police Response Time Cut to 10 Minutes, Cabinet Reports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's police response time to citizen calls has been reduced from one to three hours to just 10 minutes. The Cabinet of Ministers attributes this improvement to equipping officers with body cameras and tablets, and establishing 60 mobile police units. Specialized laboratories for DNA, fingerprint, and handwriting analysis have also been created.

item.title: Kazakh MP Proposes Review of Government Agencies for Ignoring Citizen Complaints
item.description: A member of the Kurultai, Zahira Begalieva, has proposed reviewing government bodies for their inadequate responses to citizen complaints. She noted that over five million appeals were processed via e-Otinish in 2025, with a significant number of repeated issues. Approximately 845,000 appeals came from just 1,000 individuals.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses combating human trafficking and ensuring decent work
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Commission for Combating Human Trafficking and Decent Labor held a meeting. The commission analyzed the year's work on human trafficking, labor rights protection, and decent work principles. Information from various ministries and regional commissions was heard, and future tasks were defined. Progress in aligning national legislation with ILO conventions and protecting workers' rights was noted.

item.title: Uzbek MP proposes restricting primary education in languages other than Uzbek
item.description: Uzbek MP Alisher Qodirov proposed restricting primary education in languages other than Uzbek. He linked this issue to national security and called for a review of Article 38 of the "On Preschool and Secondary Education" law, suggesting parents should not have the freedom to choose their children's language of instruction.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry attributes soldier hazing video to a joke
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense commented on a video showing a soldier being forced to sing while another wielded a belt. The ministry stated the recording was made in 2024, and the soldiers involved described the incident as a joke with no complaints. The ministry did not specify if an investigation followed the recording.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Four-Lane Highways to Reduce Fatal Road Accidents
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has proposed expanding highways to four lanes to decrease road fatalities. Following reconstruction, certain roads saw a 47% reduction in fatal accidents, according to ministry data. The aim is to design roads that prevent fatalities even in cases of driver error, particularly by reducing head-on collisions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Farmers Receive 11.9 Billion Som in Subsidized Loans Over Nine Months
item.description: In the first nine months of the year, 10,476 farmers in Kyrgyzstan received 11.9 billion som in financial support through state subsidized lending programs. The funds were allocated under projects like 'Agricultural Financing-14' (5.4 billion som), agro-industrial complex financing (5.3 billion som), and breeding stock development (1 billion som).

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Potential Data Leak Affecting 16.6 Million Citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan is investigating a potential leak of personal data from its Supreme Court's information system, with a dark web listing offering data on 16.6 million citizens. Cybersecurity firm SOCRadar discovered the listing. The authenticity of the database and any breach remain unconfirmed, though authorities are examining the allegations.

item.title: Almaty Dismantles Bus Lane for Controversial SkyTrain Project
item.description: Almaty has begun dismantling a dedicated bus rapid transit lane on Raiymbek Avenue to accommodate the planned SkyTrain monorail system. The city administration stated the move is necessary for coordination. Urban planning experts have urged reconsideration of the project, citing concerns about the assessment of alternative transportation methods.

item.title: Almaty Mountain Cluster Aims for Year-Round Tourism and Economic Growth
item.description: The Almaty Mountain Cluster project seeks to modernize existing resorts and develop a unified tourism system across five mountain areas. Its goal is to ensure year-round operation, attract investment, support entrepreneurship, and create jobs. International interest in Almaty is growing, with significant increases in flight search queries from China, the US, the UK, and South Korea.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Labor Code Now Prohibits Workplace Sexual Harassment
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially banned sexual harassment in the workplace by amending its Labor Code. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed the changes on November 13th, aligning the country's legislation with international labor standards. The new article defines sexual harassment and obligates employers to ensure a harassment-free environment. Discrimination based on skin color and political views is also now prohibited.

item.title: Suspect Arrested in Aktobe for Businessman's Murder
item.description: Police in Aktobe have arrested a suspect in the murder of a businessman, which occurred on November 16. The suspect, a resident of Aktobe and a citizen of Kazakhstan, has been placed in a temporary detention facility. The Ministry of Internal Affairs is overseeing the pre-trial investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Invests Over 11.4 Billion Som in Irrigation Sector
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated over 11.4 billion som for its irrigation sector this year, including 10.28 billion for capital investments and 1.13 billion for repairs. In 2025, 4.49 billion som are designated for irrigation. The country's irrigation canals span 28,000 km, with 5,885 km being inter-farm canals requiring annual maintenance.

item.title: Kyrgyz President and Brother Involved in Issyk-Kul Resort Ownership Dispute
item.description: A dispute over the ownership of the NOVEL Hotel & Apartments on Lake Issyk-Kul has drawn in President Sadyr Japarov and his brother, Askarbek Japarov. Businessman Kubat Alymbekov claims security officials seized the $40 million property. The State Committee for National Security states it was transferred to a Russian investor as compensation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan expects 13 million tourists by year-end, official reports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan anticipates hosting between 12.5 and 13 million foreign visitors by the end of the year, according to Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. This figure represents significant growth from previous years, with projections reaching 10.5 million by 2025. Major sporting events and new infrastructure, like the Bishkek Arena, have boosted the country's international tourism image.

item.title: Kazakhstan's '7-20-25' mortgage program conditions to remain unchanged
item.description: Kazakhstan's '7-20-25' mortgage program will continue as planned, with the National Bank allocating 100 billion tenge for financing until 2027. Conditions remain the same: a 7% annual interest rate, a 20% down payment, and a 25-year loan term. The program, launched in mid-2018, has facilitated over 87,000 mortgages totaling approximately 1.3 trillion tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Water Minister cites Chinese companies' prices more than double expected
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Water Management, Shavkat Khamraev, stated that Chinese companies CAMC and CITIC proposed prices for irrigation projects that were more than double the expected cost. Negotiations have been ongoing for over a year without resolution. The projects, involving irrigation infrastructure in several southern regions, are reportedly delayed due to these cost disputes.

item.title: World Bank Warns of Worsening Water Crisis in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Bank has warned of declining freshwater reserves and excessive groundwater extraction in Afghanistan. Since 2003, the country has lost approximately 4.9 billion cubic meters of freshwater annually, exacerbating water shortages and impacting rural livelihoods. Groundwater extraction in Kabul is nearly four times its natural replenishment rate.

item.title: Kabul Under Security Lockdown Amidst Unannounced Taliban Leader's Conference
item.description: Kabul has seen heightened security and military presence recently, coinciding with an unannounced conference on the 'Impact of the Leader's Decrees.' The event's timing and details remain unclear, with many university students and faculty reportedly unaware of or excluded from the proceedings. The university was also unexpectedly closed for a week.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Paves Over 1,800 Kilometers of Roads This Year, Exceeding Previous Year's Output
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has asphalted 1,883 kilometers of roads this year, a 1.2-fold increase compared to last year. The government allocated 69 billion soms for road infrastructure, with 56.4 billion spent. Major projects include the Barskoon-Bedel road and expansion of Bishkek's ring roads. The Kök-Art tunnel has also opened, significantly reducing travel time on the Bishkek-Osh route.

item.title: Uzbekistan Passes Law to Enhance Effectiveness of Parliamentary Inquiries
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber has passed a bill aimed at increasing the effectiveness of parliamentary inquiries. The legislation addresses instances of sluggishness in responding to deputy inquiries, proposing measures for submitting submissions to the prosecutor's office for officials who violate response deadlines. This initiative aligns with the President's 2020 address and the 2022-2026 development strategy.

item.title: New Development Bank to Provide $300 Million for Uzbekistan's Low-Carbon Energy Projects
item.description: The New Development Bank (NDB) and the Uzbek government have signed an agreement for a $300 million loan to finance the first phase of low-carbon energy development in Uzbekistan. The funds will support projects in solar, wind, hydro, and nuclear energy, aiming to reduce reliance on natural gas and enhance energy security.

item.title: Bishkek City Hall Cannot Register Converted Trolleybuses as Electric Buses
item.description: The municipality of Bishkek is facing registration issues for two trolleybuses converted into electric buses. The conversion cost approximately 4 million soms per unit. Experts deem registration impossible due to specification changes, but the city is seeking a solution. Bishkek has 65 remaining trolleybuses, with 100 transferred to Osh.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Tax Service Initiates Forced Liquidation of Inactive Companies
item.description: The State Tax Service of Kyrgyzstan has begun the third phase of forced liquidation for inactive companies and annulment of tax registrations for individual entrepreneurs. The new list includes 66,043 taxpayers, comprising 15,616 legal entities and 50,427 individual entrepreneurs who have not filed tax returns or conducted business for over a year.

item.title: KTZ IPO Prospects Complicated by Arrests, but Stability Assured
item.description: The detention of KTZ and Samruk-Kazyna heads may hinder Kazakhstan Temir Zholy's stock exchange listing preparations. Despite rising profits, KTZ faces substantial debt and a covenant breach, with an IPO considered a measure to regain lender compliance. A waiver from HSBC extends until November 30.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer at Least 50 Professions in Correctional Facilities by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to offer training in at least 50 professions in its correctional facilities by 2030, according to a presidential decree. By the 2027/2028 academic year, 310 theoretical and 420 practical training rooms will be established. The initiative aims to reduce recidivism by 30% and assist ex-convicts in finding employment.

item.title: Ipak Yuli Bank Obtains License for Islamic Banking Operations in Uzbekistan
item.description: Ipak Yuli Bank has received a license to conduct Islamic banking activities in Uzbekistan. This development allows the bank to offer Sharia-compliant financial services within the country. Further details are available through the provided link.

item.title: Kazakh MP Calls for Enhanced Security and Control in Kindergartens
item.description: A member of the Kazakh Kurultai, Tattygul Talayeva, has called for strengthened security and control measures in kindergartens, citing recent incidents of mistreatment. She highlighted that video surveillance often reveals abuse, questioning the current level of child protection. Talayeva specifically raised concerns for children with special educational needs.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced in South Korea for Funding Terrorist Organization
item.description: A South Korean court has sentenced a citizen of Uzbekistan to one year and four months in prison for financing the terrorist organization 'Katiba Tawhid wal-Jihad'. The investigation found the man made multiple money transfers to individuals linked to the group, totaling approximately $935. He was aware of the funds' intended purpose.

item.title: Tajikistan Proposes Joint Border Market with Afghanistan to Boost Trade
item.description: Tajikistan has proposed establishing a joint border market with Afghanistan to expand economic ties, despite not formally recognizing the Taliban government. The initiative aims to facilitate trade between entrepreneurs and residents of border communities. Afghan business representatives are expected to visit Tajikistan to explore investment opportunities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputies Propose Stricter Controls in Kindergartens After Child Abuse Cases
item.description: Following incidents of child abuse in kindergartens, Kazakh deputies have proposed strengthening oversight. Proposals include mandatory video surveillance in all state and private facilities, continuous audio recording in areas where video is prohibited, and extending video record retention from 30 to 90 days. Special attention is given to children with special needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Outlines Priorities Under New Constitution
item.description: Elvira Azimova, Chair of the Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan, presented annual findings on constitutional legislation, outlining priorities for further legal development under the new Constitution. She emphasized the need for systematic legislative updates and addressing legal gaps to align with new constitutional principles and values. Over 18,000 applications have been received since the court's inception.

item.title: Over 52,000 Kazakh Citizens Removed from Housing Queue
item.description: Otbasar Bank has removed over 52,500 Kazakh citizens from the housing queue after an inventory check. Changes in legislation effective September 14th allow the bank to verify applicants' data without consent. Those found to own property were removed, with further checks planned for joint ownership cases.

item.title: Afghan Parties Reject Taliban's Consultative Meetings as Ineffective
item.description: Two major Afghan political groups, the Islamic Society Party and the National Resistance Front, stated that the current crisis in Afghanistan cannot be resolved through symbolic political gatherings. They emphasized that the Afghan people desire genuine participation in governance, not just power-sharing among Taliban factions. True solutions require respecting the will of the people and ensuring their equal participation in the political structure.
